faq.a: Diyar is associated with the Arabic form دِيَار, whose core sense is diyar; abodes, lands (kurdish/arabic).

faq.q: What is the origin of Diyar?
faq.a: Diyar is associated with Arabic. Diyar is Arabic دِيَار (Diyār), the plural of دَار, meaning 'abodes, lands'. It is used as a male given name in Kurdistan.
Yes — the underlying form دِيَار is Arabic.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Diyar, diyar. Script forms are ديار, دِيَار, دیار, दियार.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
